# Requirements Document: Ordering selected offer items

## Introduction

A seller creates an order from a selection of offer items, and one request
may select from several offers.  The selection must include every item an
offer marks mandatory; the other items are optional.  The request succeeds
as a whole or is rejected as a whole.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/Creation/Create.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/airline-order-verified/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/Creation/Create.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-401

**User Story:** As a seller, I want to leave out the optional items of an offer, so that the customer pays only for what they chose.

**Rule:** WHEN a seller selects items from an offer THE SYSTEM SHALL accept the selection only if it names items the offer holds and includes every item the offer marks mandatory. (Lean: `selectItems`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. IF a selection names an item the offer does not hold THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the selection.
   - ONE-401.1, proven: proven theorem `select_rejects_unknown`; example `selectingFromTrip`
2. IF a selection leaves out an item the offer marks mandatory THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the selection.
   - ONE-401.2, proven: proven theorem `select_rejects_missing_mandatory`; example `selectingFromTrip`
3. WHEN a selection is accepted THE SYSTEM SHALL take every offer item it names and no other.
   - ONE-401.3, proven: proven theorem `select_takes_named_items`; example `selectingFromTrip`
4. WHEN a selection is accepted THE SYSTEM SHALL include at least one item the offer marks mandatory.
   - ONE-401.4, open: open theorem `select_includes_mandatory`; counterexample `seatWithoutFlight`

#### Open question on ONE-401.4

> Every accepted selection includes at least one item the offer marks
> mandatory.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guidance asks for at least one mandatory
> item in each offer and exempts a la carte offers.  When an offer marks no item
> mandatory, every selection of its items is accepted, so a seat can be ordered
> without the flight it belongs to.  The example `seatWithoutFlight` shows
> it.  Which selections are allowed from an offer that marks no item mandatory,
> and may a seat or a bag be ordered without its flight?

### Requirement ONE-402

**User Story:** As a customer, I want a trip I chose as a whole to be ordered as a whole, so that I never hold half of it.

**Rule:** WHEN a seller sends a create request with selections from one or more offers THE SYSTEM SHALL create one order holding the selected items of every offer, or reject the whole request. (Lean: `createOrder`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a create request is accepted THE SYSTEM SHALL create one order item for each item selected from each offer and none for the items left out.
   - ONE-402.1, proven: proven theorem `create_items_match_selection`; example `tripWithoutBag`
2. WHEN an order is created from offers priced in one currency THE SYSTEM SHALL make the order's total price the sum of the prices of the selected items.
   - ONE-402.2, proven: proven theorem `create_price_eq_sum`; example `tripWithoutBag`
3. IF any offer named in a create request has expired at the instant of the request THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the whole request and create no order.
   - ONE-402.3, proven: proven theorem `create_rejects_expired`; example `oneOfferExpired`
4. IF a create request selects no item from any offer THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it.
   - ONE-402.4, proven: proven theorem `create_rejects_empty`; example `nothingSelected`
5. WHEN an order is created THE SYSTEM SHALL be able to state its total price in a single currency.
   - ONE-402.5, open: open theorem `create_single_currency`; counterexample `twoCurrencies`

#### Open question on ONE-402.5

> Every order created has a total price in a single currency.
>
> Open question for the business.  Each offer is checked for its own currency,
> and a request may select from offers priced in different currencies.  The
> order then holds items in two currencies, and its item prices have no sum.
> The example `twoCurrencies` shows it: a flight priced in EUR and a hotel
> transfer priced in USD go into one order that has no total.  May one order
> hold items priced in more than one currency, and if so, what is its total?
